title: Your First 24 Hours After Shahada
whyMatters: The first day after Shahada can feel joyful, emotional, confusing, or all of those at once. This step keeps the first day simple: protect your faith, avoid pressure, and choose a few calm next actions.

exactActions.text: Pause before adding too many obligations
subSteps: Remind yourself that Islam is learned over time.
Write down two things you believe clearly right now.
Avoid internet debates and long argument threads today.
This could be a local imam, a new Muslim mentor, or a steady Muslim friend.
Ask for help learning Ghusl and the first basics of prayer.
If you do not know anyone, contact a nearby masjid or a beginner education organization.
You do not have to tell everyone immediately.
If family safety is a concern, plan before sharing.
Keep your first explanation short and personal.
Ask Allah for guidance, steadiness, and good company.
Use your own language if Arabic feels unfamiliar.

obstacles.problem: I feel pressure to become perfect right away
obstacles.solution: That pressure is not a good teacher. Start with faith, purification, prayer basics, and community support. The rest will come step by step.

obstacles.problem: I do not know who to trust
obstacles.solution: Start with identifiable organizations, a local masjid, or qualified teachers. Avoid anonymous accounts that pressure, shame, or pull you into arguments.

tinyVersion: Today, say a simple dua, choose one trusted support contact, and do not overload yourself.
unlocksNext: A calm first day makes Ghusl and the prayer on-ramp easier to approach without panic.

commonQuestions.problem: Do I need a certificate today?
commonQuestions.solution: A certificate may help for marriage, Hajj, Umrah, or some community records later, but your Islam is not dependent on paperwork. Ask a local masjid if you need documentation.

contextNotes.title: If you live with family
contextNotes.body: Do not risk your safety for an immediate announcement. Speak to a trusted mentor first if you expect hostility.

contextNotes.title: If you are alone
contextNotes.body: A single email or call to a local masjid can be enough for today. You do not need a large network immediately.

gentleScripts.title: To a mentor or masjid
gentleScripts.body: I recently became Muslim and I am looking for beginner help with Ghusl, prayer, and community support. Is there someone I can speak with?
